section.sectionSummaryBrief: Yitzchak's blessing "Vayiten Lecha" is loftier than the blessing God gave Yitzchak, which automatically extended to both sons including Esav, whereas Yaakov had to strive for this higher blessing.
section.t: Now, the blessing with which Yitzchak blessed [Yaakov], "And may God give you," is a blessing more elevated than the blessing of "And God blessed Yitzchak his son."
For the blessing with which Yitzchak was blessed by God would have been drawn to his children even if he had not blessed them,
and according to Rashi's commentary on the verse,
"And God blessed Yitzchak his son" —
that Avraham was afraid to bless Yitzchak because he foresaw that Esav would descend from him,
[so] he said, "Let the Master of blessings come and bless whomever is good in His eyes," and the Holy One, blessed be He, came and blessed him.
From this it is understood
that just as if Avraham had blessed Yitzchak,
the blessing would have been drawn also to Esav even if he had not blessed him,
so too regarding the blessing with which God blessed Yitzchak,
this blessing was drawn of itself to both his sons,
even to Esav.
But the blessing with which Yitzchak blessed [Yaakov], "And may God give you of the dew of the heavens, etc.," is a more elevated blessing.
And this is also why Yaakov exerted himself greatly and did several things not in his usual manner,
in order to receive the blessings,
even though the blessing of "And God blessed Yitzchak his son" was drawn to him of itself,
because the blessing "And may God give you of the dew of the heavens, etc." is more elevated than the blessing of "And God blessed Yitzchak his son."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Yitzchak wanted to bless Esav to elevate his lofty holy sparks, but God arranged that Yaakov receive the blessings to properly refine those sparks through him.
section.t: This will be understood by prefacing what is explained in Torah Ohr on our portion
and in several discourses,
that Yitzchak wanted to bless Esav even though he knew that the name of Heaven was not habitual in his mouth,
because Yitzchak saw that in Esav there were very high holy sparks,
and therefore he wanted to bless him,
to draw down upon him a supernal light,
through which the sparks within him would be refined.
However,
if this light had been drawn upon Esav
(not through Yaakov),
it would have been in one of two ways —
either it would have been absorbed within him, or his existence would have been nullified.
And in order that the refinement of Esav be specifically through Yaakov,
therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, arranged that Yitzchak would bless Yaakov, and the drawing down of the supernal lights
(the dew of the heavens and the fat of the land)
would be to Yaakov,
through which he would refine the sparks within Esav.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The aspect of supernal lights that refine the sparks relates to the eleven klipot, whose life-force is separate and counted as an additional entity, unlike holiness where the life-force is internal and unified.
section.t: And to understand what is the aspect of the supernal lights through which the sparks are refined,
this will be understood from what is explained in Torah Ohr there and in the aforementioned discourses,
that the klipot are in number eleven.
For in holiness the number is ten —
"ten and not nine, ten and not eleven,"
but in the side of impurity there are eleven impure crowns.
And this is also why in the incense there were eleven spices,
in order to refine the eleven impure crowns.
And that the side of impurity is in the number eleven
is
because they also count the life-force that animates them.
For in holiness, the life-force of the ten Sefiros
[and likewise every matter in holiness,
that every matter is in the number ten]
is drawn within their inwardness and is unified with them,
and therefore it is not counted by itself.
But in the side of impurity,
the life-force that animates them is separate from them
[for if it were drawn within them in their inwardness, it would be absorbed within them and would not be an aspect of life-force],
and therefore it is considered by itself.
